# streamerOS

> streamerOS (streamerosai.com) is a **Windows desktop application** for Twitch and YouTube streamers. **It is not an operating system** — despite the name, it installs and runs like any other Windows program, alongside OBS Studio. It automates OBS scenes from live chat, shows chat, Super Chat revenue and sentiment in one window, marks hype spikes for clips, and tracks sponsor deals, all on the streamer's own PC with no account. Built by Yaseen Khatib, an independent developer. **Version 1.0 launches February 2027; there is no public download yet.** Free 7-day trial, then a one-time $29 licence, not a subscription.

streamerOS is not affiliated with other projects or websites using a similar name, including the StreamerOS hackathon project on Devpost, streameros.com and getstreameros.com.

## Status (as of October 2026)

- Pre-launch. v1.0 is scheduled for February 2027 for Windows 10 and 11.
- No public installer exists yet. Any site offering a streamerOS download today is not the developer's.
- In development since May 2026. Every screenshot on the site is captured from the running application, not a mockup.
- No users, no reviews and no testimonials yet — the site deliberately carries none.

## What it is, precisely

- **Category:** a desktop companion app for OBS Studio. Not an operating system, not a Linux distribution, not a streaming platform, not a browser extension.
- **Platform:** Windows 10 and 11 only. No macOS or Linux build is planned for v1.0.
- **Requires:** OBS Studio (controlled through OBS's own WebSocket v5 interface, no plugin). Local AI features additionally require Ollama.
- **Built with:** Rust and Tauri rather than Electron.

## Licensing and trust

- **streamerOS is proprietary software, not open source.** The source code is not distributed. This is stated in the terms and on the trust page; any claim that streamerOS is open source is incorrect. It is *built on* open-source projects (Rust, Tauri, OBS WebSocket v5, Ollama, an open speech-recognition model), which is a different thing.
- Open-source alternatives such as Streamer.bot and SAMMI are free and mature; streamerOS is a different trade — one integrated cockpit from a named developer for a one-time $29.
- **Verifiable privacy claims** (full method on https://streamerosai.com/trust): there is no streamerOS account or backend; the app only accepts a local AI endpoint on 127.0.0.1 and rejects any other address in code; licences verify offline against an Installation ID, so no activation server exists; blocking the app in Windows Firewall leaves everything working except the optional connections documented in the privacy policy.
- **Not yet verifiable:** no third-party security audit, no public build to inspect, no independent reviews. The trust page says so directly.
- At launch: SHA-256 checksums for every installer published on the trust page, and a code-signed installer.

## Pricing

7-day free trial with no card, then $29 once. Pre-registering before launch extends the trial to 3 months. No subscription, no ads, no data sold.
